Hi Amit / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment going into procurement: 

Recap of what we heard:
- Primary workload: conversational triage + short-form summarization for clinical intake (avg prompt+response ~1.5k tokens).
- Expected event volume: 6M–12M requests/month initially; typical session 6–10 turns.
- Latency SLO: target p95 end-to-end <= 200ms for triage flows; background summarization can tolerate 400–600ms.
- Target unit-econ: Brightlane mentioned aiming for ~$750–$1,250 per 1M tokens as a budget band (confirm below).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm monthly token burn estimate (tokens/month) and the target $/1M token benchmark you want us to use for a formal proposal?
2) Procurement: who is the procurement contact and target PO date?
3) Attached is a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) covering milestones and a recommended configuration. Please review and suggest edits.

Why this matters (short):
- Choosing streaming vs batched inference and the service tier (hosted vs dedicated) moves both latency and unit cost significantly. We want to size the recommendation to your SLOs & budget so there are no surprises on the invoice.

I've looped in Marcus (SE) and Monica (AM) for technical/cost options.

Thanks —
Tessa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-06T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick pricing/latency sketch for Brightlane (for reply)

Tessa / Monica — drafting the numbers Amit asked for. High-level, order-of-magnitude estimates for pilot profile (~200M tokens/month):

Options (per 1M tokens, estimated):
1) Hosted — Standard (shared capacity, standard batching)
   - Cost: ~$1,100 / 1M tokens
   - Latency: p95 ~ 180–260ms (depends on burstiness).
   - Notes: cheapest short-term lift; limited SLA for p95 under heavy burst.

2) Hosted — Streaming-optimized (streaming responses, lower batch windows)
   - Cost: ~$1,450 / 1M tokens
   - Latency: p95 ~ 120–160ms for short-turn flows; better tail because of smaller batch windows and streaming kernels.
   - Notes: higher unit cost but reduces tail; good if p95 <= 150ms is required.

3) Dedicated small pool + int8 quantization (reserved capacity on GPU, tuned kernels)
   - Cost: ~$950 / 1M tokens (with reserved commit + lower per-token execution cost)
   - Latency: p95 ~ 90–140ms (best tail predictability).
   - Notes: requires monthly commit (reserved capacity) — we can structure a 3–6 month pilot commit to get to this price.

Batching trade-offs (short):
- Larger batch sizes reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead (cheaper) but increase queueing latency; for short-turn (~1.5k tokens) batching windows of 20–50ms add 20–60ms extra p95 tail depending on traffic shape.
- Streaming reduces batch wait (lower tail) but increases per-token compute overhead slightly.

Recommendation for Brightlane pilot given stated goals (p95 <= 150ms, budget ~$1k–1.2k):
- Option A (balanced): Start with Dedicated small pool trial with a 3-month commit at negotiated pricing near $1,000 / 1M tokens. Predictable tail and cost; keeps unit economics in band.
- Option B (fast start): Hosted streaming-optimized for first 4–6 weeks to validate behavior, then convert to Dedicated if tail matters to production.

I'll include a compact table in our reply to Amit showing the numbers and next steps for procurement.

— Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
